Article Title: 'Conjecture and preconceived': SC refuses to rejig panel probing police action during CJP protest
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to reconstitute a five-member high-powered committee set up to probe alleged police excesses against student protesters in Delhi, saying that the committee was formed with the highest standards of fairness and transparency.This comes after a plea was filed in the apex court alleging that one of the members of the committee was a close friend of a high functionary who is involved in the matter.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the allegations against the panel were based on “conjecture and preconceived notions” even before it had commenced its enquiry."We are not inclined to effect any alteration in the constitution of the Committee, particularly where the prayer for such reconstitution proceeds on nothing more than conjecture and preconceived notions, articulated even before the HPEC has embarked upon its enquiry," the bench said."With respect to the concerns voiced over the treatment of witnesses and of those who may wish to come forward before the HPEC to furnish their account and voice their grievances, we request the HPEC that such vulnerable witnesses be extended due protection and their identities be kept confidential and undisclosed," it added.The bench directed that Senior Advocate Monika Gusain, along with advocate C Solomon, shall assist it as a representative of the HPEC, and shall further act as an independent arbiter between the parties."Similarly, we also request the HPEC to appoint a member secretary at the earliest, so as to facilitate any such logistical or other secretarial assistance as the HPEC may require in the discharge of its functions," the bench said.Earlier, advocate Prashant Bhushan raised doubts over one of the members of the panel, who was a former DGP of a northeastern state, and said he was under a "conflict of interest" as he was a close friend of a high functionary who was likely to be under investigation.Bhushan's views were backed by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, however, opposed the reconstitution of the committee and urged the apex court to ignore such allegations.The apex court formed the HPEC, headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy, to examine allegations of police excesses against student protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest march on July 20 in Delhi and violence against police personnel.The committee comprises former Punjab and Haryana high court chief justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court judge Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP L R Bishnoi."This HPEC has been constituted bearing in mind a wide variety of considerations, including the individual expertise and experience of each of its members, as well as the diversity of the committee, among other factors," the bench had said.The July 20 march saw clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and teargas shells to disperse crowds.
Article Summary: A bench of chief justice surya kant, justices joymalya bagchi and v mohana observed that the allegations against the panel were based on “conjecture and preconceived notions” this comes after a plea was filed alleging that one of the members of the committee was a close friend of a high functionary who is involved in the matter.

Article Title: Militants torch 2 houses in Manipur village, trade fire with CRPF
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses, while security forces engaged them in an exchange of fireAccording to officials, large number of militants armed with sophisticated weapons attacked Chawangkining Naga village around 10.30pm, hours after two Kuki women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in neighbouring Tamenglong district.CRPF personnel deployed in the nearby area returned fire, triggering intermittent firing that continued for nearly six hours until around 4.30am on Wednesday."Intermittent firing was reported for nearly six hours till 4.30 am on Wednesday. The CRPF returned fire, preventing the militants from entering the village," the official said, adding that two wooden houses at the periphery of the village were, however, burnt down.The attack came hours after two Kuki-Zo women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district on Tuesday.The deceased were identified as 28-year-old nursing graduate Kimjalhai Singson and 76-year-old Phalneichong Sitlhou, both residents of the same village.Sitlhou, a widow, was shot while gathering firewood at her farm, while Singson, who had recently completed her nursing course, had returned home to help her parents with farming.Senior Naga leader and Naga Peoples' Front legislator Awangbou Newmai on Wednesday condemned the killing of the two women and the burning of houses at Chawangkining."These kinds of barbaric and senseless acts will never bring any good things to any community," Newmai said in a statement.A Kuki MLA from Saikul constituency in Kangpokpi district also condemned the killings and said one of the victims had recently graduated in nursing.Alleging the involvement of NSCN-IM and ZUF-K cadres in the killings, she said, "The killing of the innocent women is an act of sheer brutality that cannot be justified by any political cause, ideology or grievance."
Article Summary: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in manipur's kangpokpi district on tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses. The attack came hours after two kuki-zo women were shot dead at leisangphai village in neighbouring tamenglong district.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s London event called off after police raise safety concerns
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's public event outside London's iconic Shard skyscraper was cancelled after the Metropolitan Police raised concerns over crowd safety.Hundreds of fans had gathered at the venue, with several waiting for hours to see the actor-turned-politician. Vijay's team announced the cancellation over a loudspeaker, citing the lack of police permission on safety grounds.“For public safety concerns, we are calling off the programme because we don't have permission due to safety concerns,” a member of the chief minister's team said.Hours after the cancellation of the event, TVK's IT wing said in a social media post on X urged fans to refrain from waiting at the entrance of the hotel or making any attempts to meet him."We would be filled with love and heartfelt enthusiasm to meet the Tamil Nadu chief minister Thiru C Joseph Vijay. However, keeping the safety of the public in mind and considering the request of the London Metropolitan Police, an unavoidable situation has arisen where the chief minister and victorious leader cannot meet with you. Therefore, with affection, we kindly request that no one attempt to meet him," TVK's IT wing said."Furthermore, with humility, we request that you refrain from efforts such as waiting at the entrance of the hotel where the victorious leader is staying or along the route he will travel," it added.Vijay is in the UK as part of a state delegation seeking investments for Tamil Nadu. His office said earlier that the delegation had signed multiple memoranda of understanding involving investments worth around Rs 12,300 crore during the visit.The investment agreements are part of the state's effort to position Tamil Nadu as a leading advanced manufacturing and technology hub in Asia. The projects are expected to create more than 9,400 high-value jobs across the state.Vijay is scheduled to conclude his UK visit and return to India on Wednesday.

Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:
Earlier, the Bombay HC ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Salian's death.

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The central bureau of investigation (cbi) on monday registered an fir in connection with the death of disha salian, the former manager of late actor sushant singh rajput. No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the fir, based on a complaint filed by disha’s father, satish salian.

Article Title: Sanjukta Parashar first woman to head CRPF’s CoBRA commando unit
Article Text:
Sanjukta Parashar

Studied at DU, JNU

Parashar posting part of CRPF’s push to put women in lead

NEW DELHI: IPS officer Sanjukta Parashar, called the ‘Iron Lady of Assam’, has become the first woman officer to lead CRPF ’s jungle warfare commando unit, CoBRA.Parashar, a 2006-batch officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, earned the moniker of Iron Lady after leading the crackdown against militant outfit National Democratic Front of Bodoland in 2013-14 as the then Sonitpur SP.Parashar, who is from Assam, has served both in her cadre as well as in NIA, specialising in key counter-terror investigations. She was heading the CID wing of Assam Police before being appointed IG, CoBRA.She will head CoBRA at a time when the force is engaged in holding and securing large forest areas, mostly in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, reclaimed from Naxals. These operations played a key role in almost eliminating Left-wing extremism in the country by March 2026.Two battalions of the force are also posted in Manipur, which has been witnessing intermittent violence fuelled by ethnic tensions.Parashar’s appointment as IG, CoBRA is part of a larger push by CRPF to place its women officers in lead roles, including ones that are operations- and combat-heavy.“Women are heading sectors like Jammu, CoBRA, Rapid Action Force, North East, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh as IG,” a CRPF officer told TOI.A few days ago, A Vijaya Laxmi, a 2006-batch IPS officer, was posted as IG, Jammu, a sensitive sector. Nitu D Bhattacharya heads MP sector as IG and oversaw the end of Naxalism in Balaghat. Kavita Jalan, an Odisha cadre IPS officer, is heading the North East sector that includes the whole of Meghalaya and parts of Assam. Archana Shivhare, a Gujarat cadre IPS officer, is IG, Rajasthan.RAF is also led by officer Seema Dhundia, inducted in the CRPF in 1987 as part of the first batch of female officers.Parashar had, at the start of her career as an assistant commandant, handled clashes between Bodos and illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. As Sonitpur SP, she led a crackdown on NDFB, leading to the killing of 16 militants and the arrest of 64 others. Her picture leading an operation with an AK-47 in her hand earned her the title ‘Iron Lady of Assam’, as well as death threats from Bodo militants.
Article Summary: Ips officer sanjukta parashar has become the first woman officer to lead crpf’s jungle warfare commando unit, cobra. She earned the moniker of iron lady after leading the crackdown against militant outfit national democratic front of bodoland in 2013-14.

Article Title: How fish has BJP's plate full in West Bengal
Article Text:
Bengal CM prayed at Kalighat temple and had fish-basanti pulao prasad.

From Liluah to Kalighat

Dhirendra Shastri on Durga Puja.

BJP pushback

BJP dismissed all anxieties over Durga Puja.

The not-so-new ‘maach-bhaat’ row

The Bengal and Bengali dilemma for Suvendu

The larger question for BJP

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari last week offered prayers at the Kalighat Temple on the occasion of 'Kaushiki Amavasya' and partook of a traditional bhog that included fish and 'basanti pulao'. Interestingly, the timing of the visit gave the ritual a political context.The meal came amid a political controversy over Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's recent appeal to Bengali Hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. As expected, the remarks kicked up a political storm, forcing the BJP’s Bengal unit to publicly distinguish itself from Dhirendra Shastri’s position on food.Chief minister Adhikari, who had shared a stage with Shastri earlier this month and invited him to establish a centre in Bengal, then got into the balancing act.“A religious figure is entitled to express his opinion, but whether people accept it or not is a personal matter,” the chief minister said after his Kalighat visit.Adhikari also referred to his own practices, saying he follows a sattvik diet on Ashtami and during Kartik, while accepting fish offered to Goddess Kali as bhog and goat meat as prasad."A saint or a religious leader is entitled to express their opinion. People may choose to accept it or not. On Mahashtami, when I worship Maa Durga, I consume sattvik food. During the month of Kartik also, I consume sattvik food. At the same time, as a Bengali, I accept the bhog offered to Maa with fish. I also accept the prasad of goat sacrifice. Today, whatever was offered to Maa in the afternoon, the temple priests gave me the same. There was fish head and fried fish, along with basanti pulao," he said.All this began on September 4, when Adhikari shared the stage with Shastri at a Hanumant Katha programme at the Liluah Workshop Ground in Howrah.Addressing Shastri, Adhikari said: "Baba Maharaj Ji, please open a centre here. There should also be a Bageshwar Dham centre. This is the land of saints and of spiritual awakening."Two days later, on September 6, Shastri appealed to Hindus in Bengal not to sell, cook or eat non-vegetarian food near Durga Puja idols during Navratri. He described those consuming such food as "pakhandi" and called for opposition to the practice."I am appealing to the Hindus of Bengal, that during Navratri, even if you don't keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell or consume non-veg near the idols. I do not like it when dirty non-vegetarian food is eaten during Durga Puja and at gatherings linked to the festivities. I want the Hindus of Kolkata to awaken and boycott such people. These people cannot be considered religious; they are pakhandi (hypocrites). Wake up and expel those people," he appealed.The remarks triggered criticism from the opposition and prompted the Bengal BJP to distance itself from the dietary prescription.State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya said no one could decide what Bengalis should eat."How can Bengalis not have fish and meat?" he said, adding that people in Bengal would continue with their traditional food practices. He also invoked Swami Vivekananda while defending the consumption of meat and fish in Bengal’s religious traditions.Other BJP leaders, including Dilip Ghosh, also said food choices were a matter of personal preference and referred to the place of meat in some Bengali religious traditions.The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also found itself navigating the controversy following statements made during an interactive session with Kolkata puja organizers. Swami Nirgunananda, a member of the VHP's central advisory council, had suggested that non-vegetarian food stalls be kept away from the immediate area around Durga idols and situated in designated spaces outside pandals to maintain sanctity and cleanliness.When his comments were interpreted as an official organisational diktat restricting meat sales, VHP International president Alok Kumar issued a formal clarification. "Vishva Hindu Parishad has not issued any directions regarding the arrangements at Durga Puja pandals... worship of the Goddess should take place according to tradition and the atmosphere should be one of love and devotion," it said.The Kalighat temple is associated with Bengal's 'Shakta' tradition, in which offerings can include fish and meat. The bhog included several varieties of fish, along with other vegetarian dishes and goat meat.That tradition sits somewhat differently from the vegetarian dietary practices associated with Navratri in several parts of north and west India.The controversy over Shastri's remarks comes months after fish and meat had already become part of the BJP-TMC contest over Bengali identity during the assembly election campaign.Mamata Banerjee repeatedly alleged during the campaign that a BJP government would restrict what Bengalis could eat. At a rally in Purulia on March 29, she said: "BJP says can't eat fish, meat, eggs." She subsequently argued that restrictions on meat and fish sales in some BJP-ruled states showed what could lie ahead for Bengal.The issue became prominent enough for senior BJP leaders to address it directly. Amit Shah clarified that "consumption of fish, eggs will not be stopped" if the BJP came to power in Bengal, calling Mamata's claim a rumour.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also sought to engage with the issue, though from a different direction. At a rally in Haldia, he spoke about Bengal's fish production and said the state could become self-sufficient in fish under a BJP government. "In 15 years, TMC couldn't even give you fish. We created a separate ministry for fisheries," he said, contrasting Bengal's production with that of Bihar and Assam.The BJP’s campaign also included more visible efforts to counter the perception that it was opposed to Bengali food habits. Leaders publicly ate fish and meat, while BJP candidates and workers used fish in campaign imagery. On Poila Boishakh, TMC organised a "Maach-Bhaat-e-Bangali" procession, alleging that the BJP would impose restrictions on fish and meat.The argument did not remain confined to the two parties. TMC leaders presented food as part of the broader question of Bengali identity. BJP leaders, in turn, sought to emphasise that dietary choices would remain a matter of personal freedom.Months after the BJP swept Bengal in assembly elections, the opposition has sought to use the same "outsider" charge to try and alienate the saffron party from the voters. Congress filed a police complaint against Shastri, alleging that his comments hurt Bengali sentiments, while invoking the “outsider” argument that the TMC had used against the BJP during the election. Congress’s complaint described his remarks as an affront to Bengali traditions and social harmony.The TMC, which had made fish and meat part of its cultural-identity campaign against the BJP, is also again using the remark against the party.As CM, however, Adhikari has also taken a position on protests against Shastri.On September 10, he directed the Kolkata Police commissioner to arrest those who allegedly burnt Shastri’s photographs during a protest in Bhawanipur. "Not in Bengal," he said, making clear that burning photographs as a form of protest would not be tolerated.The move has produced another political contest. Congress has criticised the arrests and accused the government of protecting Shastri while acting against those protesting his remarks. One Congress leader, Atanu Das, was subsequently arrested.The recent row has brought an old question back for the BJP in Bengal: how does the party's Hindu politics sit with the state's own traditions?Bengal has a strong Shakta tradition, centred on Kali and Durga. In this tradition, the line between what is considered religious and what is considered non-vegetarian is not always drawn in the same way as it is in northern/western India. Fish, and in some places meat, can be part of offerings and rituals.That makes food an unusually sensitive issue in Bengal. And for many Bengalis, it is tied to family customs, festivals and a sense of what is distinctly 'Bengali'.Suvendu Adhikari is leading the first BJP government in Bengal. For now, he might be able to shut down critics by consuming fish bhog at Kalighat. But it will be interesting to see how he manages BJP's national Hindu politics in Bengal while also balancing the "Bengaliness".
Article Summary: Bengal cm prayed at kalighat temple and had fish-basanti pulao prasad. Bageshwar dham chief dhirendra krishna shastri's appeal to bengali hindus to refrain from eating non-vegetarian food during durga puja. The controversy over shastri's remarks comes months after fish and meat had already become part of the bjp-tmc contest over bengali identity.

NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and formed a special team to probe the death of Disha Salian, two weeks after Bombay HC ordered it to take over the case. The FIR has been filed under IPC sections covering offences such as gang rape, murder and destruction of evidence, etc.No one has been named as an accused in the case. But the FIR content, based on a complaint by Disha's father Satish Salian, mentions several people, including Aditya Thackeray, Dino Morea and Rhea Chakraborty, saying their roles need to be probed.Disha, who worked as actor Sushant Singh Rajput's manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai. Article Title: ‘Umar Khalid is a nationalist’: B K Hariprasad’s remark sparks BJP attack
Article Text:
Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a nationalist.





BENGALURU: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad Tuesday called jailed activist Umar Khalid a “nationalist” and criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University (NLSIU).“ABVP has no right to speak about Khalid because ABVP adores Nathuram Godse, who is anti-national and the first terrorist of the country,” Hariprasad said.The remarks came after ABVP in Bengaluru demanded cancellation of the proposed screening of filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s documentary, ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’, at NLSIU. The documentary was scheduled to be screened Monday by the law and society committee, a student organisation at the university. NLSIU later said it had to reschedule the event due to “logistical and security considerations”.The screening was to express solidarity with Khalid and to mark six years since his imprisonment without trial under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots.BJP hit back at Hariprasad’s remarks, calling them deeply condemnable. In New Delhi, Sambit Patra, MP, linked Hariprasad’s remarks to Congress’ past interactions with Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik.“Just think about it: this is the same Umar Khalid,” Patra said. “During the Citizenship Amendment Act protests in Feb 2020, so many people were killed in Delhi. A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.
Article Summary: Karnataka congress president b k hariprasad called jailed activist umar khalid a nationalist. He criticised akhil bharatiya vidyarthi parishad ( abvp ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at national law school of india university.

Article Title: CBI officer in RG Kar, Hathras cases assigned Disha probe
Article Text:
Disha Salian was late actor Sushant Singh Rajput's manager

NEW DELHI: Decorated CBI officer Seema Pahuja will supervise the investigation into the Disha Salian case, bringing her expertise in handling sensitive criminal inquiries to this high-profile probe, sources said. The team is set to record statements of all individuals who attended a gathering earlier that night at the Mumbai home of Rohan Roy, Disha's fiance, prior to her death on June 8, 2020.A veteran investigator, Pahuja is currently posted as an SP with the special crimes unit at the agency's headquarters in Delhi. She will be assisted by a team comprising investigating officer deputy SP Puran Kumar and others.Known for her meticulous approach and sharp forensic acumen, she has earned a formidable reputation within the investigative agency. Her stellar track record in breaking down dense evidence trails earned her the gold medal for 'best investigating officer' in 2021.Officials who have worked with her said Pahuja has been trusted with complex, sensitive, and emotionally charged cases that capture national attention through her career. Her portfolio features pivotal roles in major investigations, including the 2024 Kolkata RG Kar rape and murder case and the 2020 Hathras case."In 2017, she investigated the Unnao rape case besides another incident wherein a 16-year-old girl was raped and murdered in Shimla. The Shimla case got her widespread acclaim for using modern forensic tools to untangle a deeply challenging mystery," said an officer.Now tasked with unravelling the circumstances surrounding the 2020 death of Disha Salian, Pahuja faces a familiar territory of heavy public scrutiny. -Rajshekhar Jha
Article Summary: Seema pahuja will supervise the investigation into the disha salian case. The veteran investigator is currently posted as an sp with the special crimes unit at the agency's headquarters in delhi. She will be assisted by a team comprising investigating officer deputy sp puran kumar and others.

Article Title: Swept away by Ganga 15 days ago, Bihar woman found in UP
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: For 15 days, Sunaina Devi (55) survived on river water and the fragile shelter of a half-submerged thatched hut, after being swept 50km downstream by the monsoon-swollen Ganga. She was found alive Monday by fishermen who heard her cries.Devi, from Kapurpatti village in Bihar's Buxar district, had gone to bathe on Aug 30 when the current pulled her under. Her son, Govinda Gond, filed a missing person report at Itarhi police station. Her family did not know she had drifted across the state border into Chain Chhapra village in UP's Ballia, on the other side of the river, soon after falling in.In Chain Chhapra, Devi managed to grab an abandoned hut in a field and pull herself up. Surrounded by floodwater, she survived by drinking from the same Ganga that had nearly drowned her.On Monday she collapsed and slipped once again into floodwater. Mallah fishermen in boats heard her chants of "Shivguru-Sh-ivguru", spotted her behind sarpat grass and pulled her aboard.Hunger strike studies in British Medical Journal say with water intake, the body can survive without food for 21 to 40 days."It was miraculous," Haldi SHO Rajiv Kumar Rai told TOI. Police gave her food and water and determined her identity.The family had feared the worst. "There was no update for so many days we genuinely thought we'd lost her," Govinda said.Police said relatives broke down in tears when they saw her. "They were not expecting to find her alive. The reunion was emotional and raw," Rai said.Her husband, Janardhan, a farmer, told TOI, "Deep down, there was still a flickering hope."Devi is still dazed. "It feels like my mind stops at one place. It was very difficult to be alone for so many days. I didn't know I had such strength in me," she says.Her family says she remains weak. Doctors expect the disorientation to ease in a few days.
Article Summary: Sunaina devi (55) survived on river water and the fragile shelter of a half-submerged thatched hut. She was found alive monday by fishermen who heard her cries. Devi, from kapurpatti village in bihar's buxar district, had gone to bathe on aug 30.

Article Title: 'Fee' on UPI transactions: Modi has again surrendered to US, says Rahul
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi

New Delhi: Assailing govt over its decision to start charging for UPI transactions, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Tuesday said, "Just like with the US trade deal, compromised PM Modi is once again surrendering to American pressure. "Rahul said, "American payment companies have long opposed India's zero-MDR policy. Now, Modi govt has opened the path to changing policy in exactly that direction."Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said govt's "loot" has now reached UPI. "Sky-high inflation has emptied the common person's pocket. Wholesale inflation is near 10%, and BJP govt has planned to impose a 'Digital Payments Tax' on public, aiming to destroy whatever little savings they have left," he said.Rahul said MDR can only be levied on merchant UPI transactions, which account for 5% of volume but 65% of value. Fees on shopkeepers would eventually be passed on to customers, he added.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi slams pm modi over decision to start charging for upi transactions. "just like with the us trade deal, compromised pm modi is once again surrendering to american pressure," he said. Congress chief mallikarjun kharge said govt's "loot" has now reached upi.

NEW DELHI: A video showing Kalyan Bainsla, the car driver accused of hitting a woman biker, kneeling before his vehicle with a bandage on his hand surfaced on Tuesday.This comes as police arrested Bainsla from Rajgarh in Rajasthan, two days after his speeding Ciaz allegedly rammed into the woman’s Aprilia RS 457, causing her to skid across the road, police said.Gurgaon DCP Sandeep Kumar said on Tuesday that the accused car driver allegedly intended to kill the woman biker he rammed into on Golf Course Road. Police arrested the driver and his cousin in connection with the case.Police arrested Bainsla and his cousin, Lavish, after tracing them to Rajasthan.The DCP said attempt-to-murder charges were added based on the victim’s statement and CCTV footage, which allegedly showed Bainsla deliberately ramming his car into the woman’s bike, indicating an alleged attempt to kill her.Police also invoked Sections 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), he said. According to the DCP, Bainsla had borrowed the car from a friend and allegedly used it in the incident. Police said he runs gyms in Palwal.After giving a statement to the media, Bainsla fled to Rajasthan, where he and his cousin, Lavish, were later arrested, police said.Bainsla has denied deliberately hitting Sia, claiming that 22-23 bikers were riding aggressively, repeatedly overtaking his car and slowing down in front of it.Bainsla said Sia suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn, leaving him little time to react, and claimed he had tried to avoid the collision.He also denied fleeing the scene after the crash, saying the videos circulating on social media had been edited by stitching together separate clips.
Article Summary: Video shows accused kalyan bainsla kneeling before car with a bandage on his hand. Police arrested the driver and his cousin in connection with the case. Police said attempt-to-murder charges were added based on the victim’s statement and cctv footage.

Article Title: 'Perfect in doing drama': SC gives Rajpal Yadav final chance to deposit Rs 2 crore
Article Text:
'Perfect in doing drama': SC gives Rajpal Yadav final chance to deposit Rs 2 crore

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday gave Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav a final opportunity to deposit at least Rs 2 crore with the Supreme Court Registry within two weeks in connection with a cheque bounce case involving a private complainant.Rajpal is accused of owing Rs 5 crore to the owner of Murali Productions.Also read | Rajpal gets interim relief in cheque bounce case, SC exempts surrender if he deposits Rs 5 cr by Wednesday A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted that the actor's past conduct in the matter did not inspire confidence.However, the top court granted him two weeks after his counsel assured the bench that Rajpal would deposit at least Rs 2 crore within the deadline and provide a surety for the remaining amount.“Looking at his past conduct.. how can anybody trust him? He’s perfect in doing drama and acting in Bollywood, he’s doing same thing in Court also”, the CJI said.The court also extended the protection granted to Rajpal from arrest until the next hearing on October 5.However, it directed the actor to surrender his passport.
Article Summary: Rajpal yadav is accused of owing rs 5 crore to the owner of murali productions. Chief justice of india surya kant noted that the actor's past conduct did not inspire confidence. The top court granted him two weeks after his counsel assured the bench that rajpal would deposit at least rs 2 crore.

Article Title: Enforce speed curb device norms: SC to govts
Article Text: New Delhi: More than a decade after govt mandated installation of speed limiting devices or speed limiting functions in all public transport vehicles, enforcement remains lax, and Supreme Court Tuesday directed Centre, states and UTs to ensure compliance.Rule 118 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules provides for speed governors, and SC had passed various orders for installation of speed limiting devices. Though the SC committee on road safety had written to principal secretaries, transport secretaries and transport commissioners of all states and UTs in this regard, it was not implemented.Taking exception, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said the law had been framed by Centre and govt had to take steps to implement the statutory provision."Why does govt need directions from the court? These are statutory provisions and rules," the bench said.
Article Summary: Rule 118 of central motor vehicles rules provides for speed governors. Sc had passed various orders for installation of speed limiting devices. Justices j b pardiwala and k v viswanathan said the law had been framed by centre and govt had to take steps to implement.

Article Title: Multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests, better centres top reform wish list
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A single bad day should not decide a student's future - and a poorly equipped examination centre should not ruin it. These concerns feature in thousands of suggestions received by the high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's examination system.The panel, led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders ahead of its next meeting, scheduled after the Brics summit. It will begin examining reform proposals, sources said.Constituted amid paper leaks, cancelled tests and infrastructure failures, the task force is examining examination security, technology, infrastructure, accessibility, student well-being and testing-agency reforms. Suggestions invited from citizens until Sept 13 will be compiled into a detailed report. A prominent demand is to give candidates multiple attempts at high-stakes entrance tests.Manojranjan Nayak, founder-president of Siksha 'O' Anusandhan, a deemed-to-be university, said: "Examination reform must move beyond making a flawed system more efficient. Multiple attempts can reduce the disproportionate cost of one bad day, but they should be combined with secure, accessible and uniformly equipped centres, transparent evaluation and greater weight for sustained learning.Technology can improve reliability, but it must not create a new divide between candidates with different levels of digital access. The real test of reform is whether every student, regardless of geography or income, gets a fair and dignified opportunity to demonstrate ability."Poor infrastructure at testing centres is another concern. Examinations at a Jaipur centre were disrupted by power failures on two consecutive days, affecting candidates and raising questions about how centres are selected and monitored.“For a young candidate, exam day carries years of preparation and the hopes of an entire family. If an examination is disrupted because the centre loses power or connectivity, it is not a small technical failure; it is the candidate who pays the price,” said Ashish Mittal, founder and managing director of Innovatiview.“That is why India needs Adarsh Pariksha Kendras, where reliable power, secure internet, tested computers, biometric verification and CCTV are basic standards, not last-minute arrangements. Every candidate deserves a fair examination in a centre that will not fail them,” he added.The issue is more urgent as agencies expand computer-based testing. The National Testing Agency has written to education ministry organisations seeking suitable centres. At its request, the All India Council for Technical Education has asked government technical institutions for details of computers, internet connectivity, power backup, CCTV and vacant spaces that could become standard testing centres.The government is identifying more public institutions to host entrance examinations from the next academic cycle, reducing dependence on private centres and building a more reliable national testing network.
Article Summary: High-powered task force set up to overhaul india's examination system. Panel, led by infosys co-founder nandan nilekani, has been consulting stakeholders. Constituted amid paper leaks, cancelled tests and infrastructure failures.

Article Title: Balakrishnan panel unlikely to propose inclusion of converts in SC list
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A special panel may recommend to the govt that status quo should be maintained on the definition of Scheduled Castes, as laid down by the Presidential (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, and not expanded to bring in Dalit converts to Islam and Christianity.The commission of inquiry, headed by former Chief Justice of India KG Balakrishnan, has been mandated to investigate if status of Scheduled Castes can be extended to persons who have converted to religions other than those eligible for it - popularly known as "Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam".The 1950 Presidential Order states that only persons belonging to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism can be members of Scheduled Castes.The vexed issue has been pending before Supreme Court for over 20 years in which "Dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the Scheduled Castes' list.Reports of the past commissions - Kaka Kalelkar, Sachar and Rangnath Misra - on the tricky issue, and the stand taken by National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) over the years have provided the background material for research. A 1911 book by a Christian missionary has also been relied upon.While Sachar did not recommend the Scheduled Castes status for religious converts, Misra panel did ask for the Scheduled Castes' list to be made religion-neutral. Its recommendation was apparently not accepted by govt because the panel did not conduct a study to reach its conclusion. Kalelkar commission, sources said, recommended only OBC status, and not Scheduled Castes recognition to Dalit converts.NCSC took a contradictory stand during the UPA govt, even mentioning that 50% cap on reservations should not be disturbed.According to sources, the 1911 book states that Dalits gain social status after conversion - something which seems to lighten the burden of disability which is cited for giving affirmative action benefits to Scheduled Castes. Given the inputs, the commission may recommend that the present arrangement on eligibility for inclusion in Scheduled Castes' list should stay. Besides, there is also a lack of clarity on which of the religious converts were formerly members of Scheduled Castes, sources said.Pending for over two decades, the demand of religious converts to be included in Scheduled Castes' list has become controversial because of its political dimensions. Existing Dalit communities are often found to oppose fresh inclusions in Scheduled Castes' list, arguing that such a move will increase the number of claimants for job and educational reservations.BJP argues that making Scheduled Castes status religion-neutral will encourage religious conversions.
Article Summary: The 1950 presidential order states that only persons belonging to hinduism, sikhism and buddhism can be members of scheduled castes. The vexed issue has been pending before supreme court for over 20 years in which "dalit converts" have demanded that they be included in the list.

Article Title: SC junks ex-Delhi mayor's plea for FIR on UP cops
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: SC Tuesday refused to entertain former Delhi mayor Farhad Suri's plea for an FIR against UP police for conducting a midnight raid at his city home in search of journalist and Ram temple donation pilferage whistleblower Abhishek Upadhyay.Suri's counsel, Anoop Awasthi, told SC that a Ghaziabad police team had raided Suri's Nizamuddin East residence on the night of Aug 22 without disclosing warrants and corresponding entries at Nizamuddin police station. He urged the CJI Surya Kant-led bench to lay down guidelines for the police department of a state conducting midnight raids in another state.UP additional advocate general Sharan Dev Singh Thakur said Suri's petition was an abuse of the process of law and "unnecessary sensationalisation" as police merely rang the bell to find out whether Upadhyay, who was wanted in a road rage case in Ghaziabad, was available at his place. They left after Suri denied Upadhyay's presence, Thakur said, adding that Suri could approach senior police officers for registration of an FIR and, if dissatisfied, he could move a trial court with a private complaint against police.As Suri wanted the FIR to be lodged in Delhi, the bench disposed of his petition by giving him liberty to approach the Nizamuddin police station for filing a complaint against the officers who raided his home unauthorisedly. SC had on Aug 25 protected Upadhyay against arrest by Ghaziabad police. tnn
Article Summary: Supreme court refuses to entertain former delhi mayor farhad suri's plea for an fir against up police. Up additional advocate general sharan dev singh thakur said the petition was an abuse of the process of law and "unnecessary sensationalisation" sc had on aug 25 protected upadhyay against arrest by ghaziabad police.

Article Title: SC bins ex-NSE chief Chitra Ramakrishna's plea to stop graft proceedings
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday rejected the plea of former National Stock Exchange (NSE) managing director and chief executive officer (CEO) Chitra Ramakrishna challenging proceedings against her under the Prevention of Corruption Act.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran refused to interfere with a Delhi high court order which had allowed her prosecution. The court, however, allowed her to raise before the trial court the question whether she was performing a public duty and could be treated as a public servant to be brought within the purview of the anti-corruption law. "We are of the view that no error could be said to have been committed by HC in passing the impugned judgement.The petitioner was the MD and CEO of NSE. Her argument is that the NSE being a private/non-govt company, it cannot be said that the petitioner was discharging a public duty."The case against Ramakrishna stems from a Feb 11 order of the Securities and Exchange Board of India which said she was allegedly involved in financial irregularities related to fixation and frequent revision of compensation of former NSE employee Anand Subramanian.
Article Summary: Former national stock exchange (nse) managing director and chief executive officer (ceo) chitra ramakrishna challenging proceedings against her. Justices j b pardiwala and k vinod chandran refused to interfere with a delhi high court order which had allowed her prosecution.

Article Title: ED puts lens on IBC frauds, including excessive haircuts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Enforcement Directorate will start a drive against fraud under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code , including cases of alleged collusive resolutions involving disproportionately large haircuts which helped defaulting promoters re-acquire assets.In a direction to zonal offices during a three-day high-level meeting of the agency's special directors in Bengaluru, ED director Rahul Navin asked them to initiate money laundering investigations against chief protagonists of resolutions which are prima facie dubious but were cleared by National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)."Identify red flags, obtain copies of applications related to preferential, undervalued, fraudulent and extortionate transactions from resolution professionals, file intervention applications before the tribunal, and initiate independent investigations under PMLA against masterminds," he is learned to have told his senior colleagues.The decision to crack down on alleged cases of fraudulent re-acquisition of assets through NCLT, manipulating voting by front entities forming a majority in a committee of creditors, has come at a time when ED is looking into prominent cases. Ownerships of some linked bankrupt companies were allegedly transferred to front entities after creditor banks took haircuts for up to 97-99% of the admitted claims.ED is examining interplay of IBC and PMLA, particularly "the legal tension between the moratorium under Section 14 and the immunity under Section 32A of the code on the one hand, and attachment powers under PMLA on the other".
Article Summary: Enforcement directorate will start a drive against fraud under insolvency and bankruptcy code. Cases of alleged collusive resolutions involving disproportionately large haircuts which helped defaulting promoters re-acquire assets. Ed director rahul navin asked them to initiate money laundering investigations against chief protagonists.
